metadata.dataset_name: Sri Lanka Rice Disease Advisory Knowledge Base
metadata.institute: Rice Research and Development Institute (RRDI), Bathalagoda
metadata.purpose: Disease management and advisory information for a paddy disease detection application
metadata.source_policy: Information is based primarily on Sri Lanka Department of Agriculture RRDI disease-management information.
metadata.important_note: Disease identification from an image should be treated as a screening result. Field history, field symptoms, plant symptoms and expert diagnosis may be required for accurate diagnosis.

diseases.life_stage: Any life stage of the rice plant
symptoms: Blackening and rotting of infected nodes
Panicle base infection can cause neck rot and panicle falling
Severe infection may produce partly filled grains or whiteheads
prevention: Apply nitrogen according to recommended rates or leaf colour chart guidance
Improve soil condition using burnt paddy husk during land preparation where recommended

nitrogen: Use leaf colour chart guidance where appropriate
fertilizer.reason: RRDI identifies excessive nitrogen application as a condition favoring rice blast.

products_listed_by_rrdi.rrdi_rate: 11 g or 11 ml in 16 L of water

chemical.safety_note: Chemical recommendations should be verified against the current Sri Lankan registered-product label and current Department of Agriculture recommendations before being presented as an application instruction.

monitoring: Check leaves regularly for spindle-shaped lesions
Monitor fields during high-humidity conditions
Monitor during periods of low night temperature
Pay particular attention where excessive nitrogen has been applied
Monitor susceptible varieties
Monitor nodes and panicles as the crop develops
next_season_management: Add burnt paddy husk during land preparation where recommended

symptoms: Wilting and yellowing of leaves at seedling stage
Wilting of seedlings known as kresek
Yellowish bacterial ooze may be observed from cut leaf ends
Water-soaked orange stripes on mature leaves
Lesions may begin at leaf tips
Lesions may progress toward the leaf base
prevention: Prevent drainage water from infected fields entering disease-free fields
Use appropriate potassium management when disease is observed

nitrogen: Use leaf colour chart guidance where appropriate
potassium: Potassium fertilizer may be used to help manage further disease spread after disease is observed, according to RRDI guidance

water_management: When disease is observed, stop water supply and allow the field to dry
Where complete water removal is not possible, use drainage ditches or water courses
Avoid directing drainage water from infected fields into disease-free fields

chemical.fungicide_recommendation: Do not automatically recommend a fungicide because this is a bacterial disease.
chemical.instruction: Use integrated disease-management practices and current Sri Lankan Department of Agriculture recommendations.

monitoring: Check seedlings for wilting and yellowing
Check mature leaves for water-soaked orange stripes
Monitor during continuous heavy rain
Monitor during high-humidity conditions
Monitor fields where excessive nitrogen has been applied
Check drainage water movement between fields

diseases.life_stage: More prevalent as plants approach maturity
symptoms: Small dark brown to reddish-brown spots
Light-weight or chalky kernels may develop

nitrogen: Use leaf colour chart guidance where appropriate
general: Maintain adequate and balanced plant nutrition
Improve soil fertility where nutrient deficiency is present
Consider soil conditions such as salinity and iron toxicity when interpreting disease risk

soil_management: Improve soil quality using organic fertilizer
Add burnt paddy husk during land preparation where recommended
Consider soil salinity and iron toxicity
seed_management: Hot-water treatment of seed at 53-54°C for 10-12 minutes

chemical.instruction: RRDI recommends seed treatment with a seed-protectant fungicide as one management option. Any product and application rate should be verified against current Sri Lankan registration and recommendations.

monitoring: Check leaves regularly for brown circular or oval lesions
Monitor seedlings for seedling blight
Monitor crop approaching maturity
Monitor fields with nutrient-deficient soils
Monitor fields affected by salinity
Monitor fields affected by iron toxicity
Monitor during high-humidity conditions
Monitor crops experiencing drought stress
next_season_management: Apply organic fertilizer to improve soil quality
Add burnt paddy husk during land preparation where recommended
Treat seed with hot water where appropriate
